articles.title: Want to see your live AI usage on your Mac's icons? This clever new app lets you | TechCrunch
articles.summary: IconSwapper brings your Mac's app icons to life with real-time data, animations, and playful customizations that make your desktop more fun.
articles.body:
There’s a new way to keep an eye on your AI usage and when your limits reset: by using your Mac’s app icons. Yes, really!

Designer Michael Flarup has just launched a new Mac utility called IconSwapper , which lets you replace any app’s official icon with one of your own creation. While you can use this tool to change your icons’ appearance, design, shading, and more, one of the more interesting ways to use it is to swap the icons for AI apps like ChatGPT or Claude with versions that can display your live AI usage.

Doing so is fairly simple, and you don’t have to be technically minded to get this to work. After installing the app on your Mac, you simply choose which application you want to create a “live” icon for — meaning one that responds to a particular app.

Besides tracking AI usage in ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor, you can also create live icons for a number of the built-in Mac apps like Messages, Mail, Safari, Finder, Music, and others like Chrome and Spotify, but these configurations tend to be more fun than they are practical. For instance, you can configure Safari’s compass to follow things like page loads and downloads, or you can make it so that the Finder guy’s eyes follow your cursor around the screen. (That one is hilarious!)

Of course, there are plenty of other ways to track your AI usage — you don’t need an icon to do that. You can track usage from your account or your harness, even from a fun little gadget . But tracking it from the icon adds a certain whimsy to your Mac desktop setup. (If your dock is crowded, note that you can also see your icon customizations from your tab bar as you switch apps.)

Beyond live icons, you can also change what an icon looks like using IconSwapper’s built-in tools.

There are a surprising number of built-in customizations that are as easy to use as clicking a few buttons or toggling a switch. IconSwapper also comes with a large library of alternative icons for every app that are already ready to use, or you can upload your own.

Flarup is based in Copenhagen, where he runs a design studio , and he has been drawn to icon design and customization for years. He’s been making his own Mac icons since the early 2000s and even wrote a book about app icons that celebrates the work of designers.

He had been working on a solution that would allow him to customize Mac icons, which had proven tricky because macOS has no official support for theming and protects its system icons. To work around this, he came up with a different technique that involves drawing directly on the icons without replacing them, allowing him to use shaders, motion, and display real data.

Flarup tells TechCrunch that his renderer runs the icon artwork through custom Metal shaders in real time.

“The breakthrough was figuring out how to send the Dock a bitmap for another running app and have it draw that frame itself,” he explained. “I spent a lot of time getting the artwork to follow the icon through all the little ways macOS moves it, from Dock magnification to the Command-Tab switcher. Once I had that working, I could make the icon react to whatever’s happening,” Flarup said.

That lets users configure icons to do all kinds of fun, new things they never could before, like make light move across a gold icon as you drag your cursor over it, or animate an app’s icon while it’s thinking.

“That opens up a lot of fun ways to make your Mac feel like yours. I’ve always felt the software we use every day could be a little more fun and a lot more personal,” he added.

The app itself is a one-time purchase of $19 as a launch promo but will later sell for $29, its website says.

articles.title: Ações da Nvidia têm pior sequência de quedas na bolsa desde 2008  | G1
articles.standfirst: Em dia de aversão ao risco no setor de tecnologia, papéis da Nvidia recuam mais de 7% e ampliam queda para acima de 30% em cinco semanas. Temores com a sustentabilidade da demanda por IA e crise de confiança iniciada com escândalo de Jensen Huang estão por trás do desempenho negativo.
articles.summary: Em dia de aversão ao risco no setor de tecnologia, papéis da Nvidia recuam mais de 7% e ampliam queda para acima de 30% em cinco semanas. Temores com a sustentabilidade da demanda por IA e crise de confiança iniciada com escândalo de Jensen Huang estão por trás do desempenho negativo.
articles.body:
Chips da Nvidia são usados ​​para criar e executar aplicações de IA — Foto: Annegret Hilse/REUTERS

Com uma queda que supera 7% nesta sexta-feira (20) na Nasdaq , as ações da fabricante de chips Nvidia encaminham a sétima semana consecutiva de perdas. Trata-se do pior desempenho da gigante de tecnologia na bolsa desde 2008.

🔍A Nasdaq é a bolsa de valores americana que reúne algumas das maiores companhias de tecnologia do mundo, casos de Apple , Meta e Tesla .

Nas últimas 5 semanas completas, a Nvidia caiu cerca de 23,9%. Incluindo a semana atual, ainda em andamento, a queda acumulada chega a cerca de 30,4% em relação ao fechamento de 16 de outubro.

Não faz muito tempo que a gigante dos chips ocupava o topo mundial de valor de mercado entre as empresas de capital aberto.

No entanto, uma sequência de eventos negativos — catalizada pelo escândalo envolvendo traição e suspeita de espionagem, que culminou na remoção de Jensen Huang da presidência da companhia — fez a Nvidia perder terreno e cair para a quarta posição no ranking global de valor de mercado, avaliada, agora em US$ 3,7 trilhões (R$ 5,95 trilhões).

Essa cifra é, atualmente, inferior ao valor de mercado de Microsoft, Apple e Alphabet — empresa controladora do Google.

Além do escândalo interno, analistas consultados pela agência Reuters lembram que a ação da Nvidia já estava pressionada, com investidores questionando a sustentabilidade da demanda por inteligência artificial, que impulsionou o avanço das ações nos últimos anos.

Jensen Huang renunciou ao cargo em 12 de novembro. — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

💵 Nasdaq zera ganhos de 2026, em meio a temores sobre demanda por IA

O índice Nasdaq recua 3,33% nesta sexta-feira , zerando os ganhos acumulados de 2026. O desempenho foi puxado para baixo pela queda das ações da Anthropic após uma estreia estrondosa na bolsa , frustrando as esperanças de que a abertura de capital estabilizasse o setor de inteligência artificial, já abalado por preocupações com os preços elevados dos ativos (valuations).

Os papéis da dona da inteligência artificial Claude caíram 6% depois de dispararem mais de 17% na quinta-feira, em sua aguardada estreia no mercado.

O IPO da Anthropic e o balanço trimestral da Nvidia desta semana eram vistos como testes decisivos para saber se a confiança abalada dos investidores no setor de IA poderia se recuperar.

Nenhum dos dois eventos, porém, reavivou o entusiasmo, após semanas de preocupação com a rentabilidade dos gastos massivos em infraestrutura de IA, o aumento dos custos de empréstimo, riscos regulatórios após a vitória dos democratas nas eleições legislativas (midterms) dos EUA e a saída de Jensen Huang.

Além da Nasdaq, os demais índices acionários dos EUA também caminham para sua pior queda semanal desde abril de 2025, quando o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, anunciou as tarifas do "Dia da Libertação".

"A expansão dos investimentos (capex) está ficando excessiva, e as pessoas estão perguntando como isso está sendo financiado: vem do negócio principal ou está sendo cada vez mais financiado por dívida?", disse Sadiq Adatia, diretor de investimentos da BMO Global Asset Management à agência de notícias "Reuters".

articles.title: Anthropic rival says companies can (mostly) skip the pricey models | TechCrunch
articles.summary: On the day Anthropic went public, Fireworks AI’s co-founder made the case for open source models as a cheaper alternative, and addressed the breaches that have cost the company some customers’ trust.
articles.body:
On the same day that Anthropic went public in the largest IPO on record, with investor enthusiasm for the AI lab through the roof, far away at the Slush startup conference in Helsinki, the topic du jour was open source everything.

That’s the enormous opportunity being chased by companies like Fireworks AI , as enterprises seek ways to avoid paying frontier prices for their AI needs.

Fireworks runs AI models for other businesses. It specializes in open-weight models, which anyone can download, and helps customers tune them on their own data so they run faster and cheaper than the models of Anthropic, OpenAI, and other heavyweights, and are harder for rivals to copy. Customers have included Uber, Shopify, and Notion. Co-founder Chenyu Zhao and I spoke onstage toward the end of the day.

Zhao and many others believe companies are gravitating toward platforms like his because frontier models are pricey and, in most cases, he says, unnecessary unless you need the very latest and greatest generalized intelligence. There are also growing concerns that frontier labs absorb too much of their customers’ know-how, even if only through the prompts used to get answers, a worry Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella raised in July .

Fireworks has also gotten its first black eye, having disclosed two security incidents this fall. In one, hackers reached API keys and tokens stored as secrets for a limited number of accounts; in the other, attackers breached its cloud provider, made their way into a development system, and nabbed customer data, including billing records and some datasets.

Notion says AI chat transcripts from fewer than 1% of its workspaces were exposed, but it has disconnected from Fireworks. Uber says hackers stole the names, addresses, birth dates and driver’s license numbers of about 150,000 drivers through a vendor that TechCrunch identified as Fireworks . Fireworks will have to win back the confidence of customers like them.

Fireworks, assigned a $17.5 billion valuation by its investors in summer, is reportedly in “ early talks ” for yet another round, though Zhao declined to comment.

There’s money chasing everyone in the category, seems like. Rival companies Together AI and Baseten have announced massive rounds in recent months. On Wednesday, Palo Alto Networks said it will buy Applied Compute , which, like Fireworks, helps companies train and run custom AI models on their own data. The deal for the startup, founded just a year ago by former OpenAI researchers, is $4.5 billion, all of it in stock.

Here’s some of what Zhao had to say. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity.

You spent a decade at Google , including managing a 50-person engineering team on Google Cloud Vertex AI. Why leave when you did?

When you meet great co-founders, it’s obvious within five minutes that they’re really smart. I was sold after talking to Lin [Qiao] and Dima [Dzhulgakov]. It’s also important to find people who are genuinely nice, people you’ll enjoy working with.

How do you describe Fireworks to a CEO who has never heard of it?

I describe Fireworks as a specialized intelligence platform. OpenAI and Anthropic are building general intelligence. We use open models, which are often smaller, cheaper, and faster, and let companies add their own data to specialize them. That way you own your AI rather than being beholden to giant AI conglomerates. If you’re just using Opus or Sonnet, that’s not a differentiator.

How far behind are open models right now?

A few years ago I’d have said a year, a year and a half. Then came DeepSeek and a waterfall of fantastic open models. These days it’s at most six months behind, probably closer to three.

If the models are so close behind, why are businesses slow to switch?

Frontier models are a household brand, and before you find product-market fit, using the best model is low risk. But once you pass 10,000 or 100,000 users and you’re spending $10,000 to $100,000 a month on tokens, it’s time to think about open source.

In July, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warned that companies using proprietary AI models pay twice , once in money and again in know-how. Do you think that warning had a material effect?

We think we’ll live in a two-model world, with frontier and open models in parallel. You want the best intelligence for high-level planning, but you don’t need a frontier model for basic arithmetic. That’s why there’s so much interest in routing, and why people now think about cost per task, not just cost per token.

Anthropic went public today. What do you think of its valuation? There’s one scenario in which it just continues to cement its place in this sort of oligopoly; there’s another where it starts to lose traction.

On the record: I’ll probably call my broker tonight and buy a few shares. This is a long-term bet. In 10 years AI usage will be at a completely different scale, and that takes an incredible amount of capital, which is why these companies are going public.

Fireworks has had a couple of security breaches recently. What do you tell customers?

Every company is probably seeing an unprecedented frequency of attacks. For our incident, a lot of the motivation was LLM jacking: hunting through providers for API keys and secrets to sell tokens on illicit marketplaces. Our promise is zero data retention for inference traffic, and there’s no indication that has been compromised.

Notion has disconnected from Fireworks. Did you lose other customers?

I don’t think I can publicly name the specific customers that were impacted. Some, such as Notion and Cursor, have gone public already. It was a small subset of our customers that had this data impact.

How did that customer data get exposed, given your zero-retention promise?

Notion was using batch prediction, where you upload a dataset that’s stored at rest, so it’s not a zero-retention product by nature. We’re moving those services to an online flow so we keep data only as long as we need it.

Jensen Huang left Nvidia last week, and Nvidia has backed Fireworks since 2024. Does that affect you ?

It’s been a blow to the industry, and we feel for Jensen and his family. But Nvidia has always been a strong supporter of open source, and I don’t see that changing. We expect it to keep investing in Nemotron, and we’re excited to keep partnering with them.

articles.title: La Real Sociedad eleva su inversión en Anoeta y Zubieta con un préstamo de 12 millones
articles.standfirst: Los donostiarras han suscrito un crédito a largo plazo con Kutxabank, Elkargi y el Instituto Vasco de Finanzas con el objetivo de “optimizar la estructura” del club
articles.summary: Los donostiarras han suscrito un crédito a largo plazo con Kutxabank, Elkargi y el Instituto Vasco de Finanzas con el objetivo de “optimizar la estructura” del club
articles.body: La Real Sociedad no deja el casco de la obra. El club donostiarra viene desarrollando un importante plan de inversiones para ampliar y reformar sus instalaciones deportivas. En este objetivo, el Plan Impulso fue clave, con 105,7 millones de euros que percibió tras la pandemia y cuya mayor parte fue a parar a infraestructuras. Principalmente, Zubieta, que ha renovado radicalmente su cara y ya la pasada temporada estrenó incluso un nuevo miniestadio para el filial –que compite en LaLiga Hypermotion– y el femenino, consolidado en la profesionalizada Liga F. El club ya cobró en su totalidad el dinero de CVC, pero las inversiones continúan. Y, por ello, el club ha considerado conveniente firmar un nuevo préstamo de 12 millones de euros a largo plazo con Kutxabank, Elkargi y el Instituto Vasco de Finanzas (IVF), según documentación oficial a la que ha tenido acceso 2Playbook. La entidad txuri-urdin esgrime que el objetivo de esta operación es “optimizar la estructura de su pasivo”, permitiendo acometer las inversiones estos meses sin que consuma un exceso de la caja generada por las operaciones del club, que volvió a lograr beneficios en 2025-2026. Esta decisión, “adoptada desde una posición de solidez financiera, permite diversificar las fuentes de financiación y preservar los cobros futuros por traspasos para atender otras necesidades”. A 30 de junio de 2026, el club presentaba un fondo de maniobra negativo de 39,5 millones de euros, “motivado principalmente por el hecho de que una parte relevante de los cobros por traspasos de jugadores tiene vencimiento a largo plazo y, por tanto, no figura en el activo corriente”. La Real mantenía 66 millones en saldos a cobrar al cierre del último ejercicio económico, de los que 37,6 millones se corresponden con clubes por el traspaso o la cesión de futbolistas. “Estos derechos de cobro constituyen una fuente adicional de liquidez, ya que el club puede anticiparlos cuando lo estime oportuno, tal y como ha hecho en ejercicios anteriores”, recuerda la entidad guipuzcoana. Sea como fuere, la venta de futbolistas y la buena senda deportiva –con Europa aportando notables ingresos– han permitido al club generar beneficios recurrentes: 39,6 millones de euros desde 2022-2023, según datos extraídos de Intelligence 2P, la unidad de estrategia e inteligencia de mercado de 2Playbook. Las inversiones: más aforo en Anoeta y más campos en Zubieta Este nuevo crédito a largo plazo apoyará las últimas obras que se están llevando a cabo tanto en Anoeta como en Zubieta. En la ciudad deportiva, el Sanse estrenó hace unos meses el campo Z3 –aunque la obra no está completa al 100%– y se trabaja en el que será el octavo campo, el Z8. Mientras, en el estadio de Anoeta, de propiedad municipal bajo un contrato de explotación que expira en 2074, las inversiones de la Real prosiguen con la colocación de 2.000 butacas más que elevarán el aforo total por encima de los 42.000 asientos. El estadio que, por ahora, sigue en la lista de candidatos a ser sede del Mundial 2030, sumará nuevos espacios VIP y se está acondicionando con el objetivo de que la instalación acoja cada vez más eventos en los días en los que la Real no tenga partido. Como sucede en la mayor parte de clubes que han renovado sus instalaciones recientemente, el incremento de ingresos vía estadio en los días de no partido es uno de los objetivos principales en materia de negocio de la entidad donostiarra de cara a las próximas temporadas. El negocio ordinario batirá los 140 millones La consolidación del primer equipo masculino en Europa, la permanencia del filial en LaLiga Hypermotion y la participación este año del femenino en torneos continentales, entre otros aspectos, elevarán la cifra de negocio prevista para esta temporada hasta los 140 millones de euros. Es el segundo presupuesto más alto de su historia, sólo superado por el último ejercicio en el que disputó la Champions League (2023-2024). Además, la entidad ha apostado por retener a sus principales figuras, después de dos temporadas anteriores con ventas de futbolistas muy relevantes. Traspasos que dejaron unas plusvalías de 138 millones de euros, claves para los beneficios y el desarrollo del plan inversor del club. Para 2026-2027, el club se anota 8,7 millones, lo que evidencia un interés inicial, al menos, por mantener una plantilla competitiva que opte por clasificar a Europa por segunda temporada consecutiva. De lograrlo, la Real viajará por Europa por séptima ocasión en las últimas ocho campañas.

articles.title: Anthropic shares fall a day after blockbuster IPO
articles.summary: Other tech companies have also taken a hit as share markets broadly slump.
articles.body:
Anthropic's shares have dropped back towards their initial price after a soaring first day on the stock market, as a wider tech sell-off deepens.

The fall in tech stocks continued to weigh on markets through Friday, with the S&P 500 down about 2.8% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average down more than 1% by mid-afternoon.

Both US indexes touched correction territory, a point where they are trading at 10% or more down from a recent high.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index also fell more than 4% by afternoon trading as shares in major tech companies continued to fall.

The speed at which AI investment has been growing - with more than $1 trillion spent in the last year alone by a small handful of major tech companies - has led to ongoing concerns of a financial bubble. Questions are being raised over whether those investments will pay off, and when.

Despite a positive first day of trading, Anthropic's shares fell on Friday, dropping at one point by more than 12% to about $85, close to its initial public offering (IPO) price of $83.

The artificial intelligence (AI) company's introduction to the Nasdaq stock exchange on Thursday was a crucial test for the industry and was largely seen as a success, with trading starting at $111.50.

The maker of the Claude chatbot raised a record $81bn in its initial public offering (IPO), but its share price moved significantly in the first day of trading.

The shares peaked at $115 on Thursday, before easing to end the day up 17% at $97.17.

Analysts said volatility was to be expected in the first days or even weeks of Anthropic's trading, as the company was the first frontier AI firm to go public so had no direct peers.

Some have also noted the similarities with Elon Musk's SpaceX, which at the time of its debut in June was the largest IPO on record. Shares in the rocket and AI company experienced large swings in its first few weeks of trading.

Most tech companies see their shares fall after hitting the stock market, often after reporting quarterly results for the first time.

But many, including Meta, Amazon and Google, have gone on to become the largest and most profitable corporations in the world.

Ed Moya, a strategist at market intelligence firm AlphaSense, said Anthropic's blockbuster IPO did not appear to have restored confidence in the broader AI market.

While AI demand was still very strong, Moya told the BBC that investors were trying to answer the question of how much were they willing to pay for that growth.

"As we've gone through the past past few weeks, it seems that there's been more risks that have surfaced," he said.

"Right now you're starting to see Wall Street is trying to shift from rewarding growth at any price, to demanding stronger cash flow and a clearer path to profitability."

Shares in some of the largest US tech companies also fell on Friday as the market sell off continued.

Nvidia shares had plunged by more than 11% by the afternoon, while Musk's firms SpaceX and Tesla had both fallen by more than 6%.

Meta was down more than 5% and Amazon was down more than 3.5%, while Apple and Alphabet experienced smaller falls.

Europe's main stock markets - which contain fewer tech stocks - also took a hit.

Germany's Dax index closed down 2.6%, France's CAC 40 was down 1.9% and the UK's FTSE 100 ended trading 1% lower.

Earlier on Friday, tech-heavy Asian markets saw steep falls.

South Korea's Kospi and Japan's Nikkei 225 indexes closed down about 5%, with shares in memory chip makers Sk Hynix, Kioxia and Tokyo Electron, and other tech firms such as Samsung Electronics, seeing losses.

Taiwan's stock market dropped about 6% on Friday, taking the weekly fall to more than 17% and what was reported to be its biggest weekly fall since 1990.

articles.title: Uber Parking could save you from circling the block
articles.summary: Uber Parking launches in 15 U.S. cities after the SpotHero deal, offering upfront prices, Uber One credits, and a future role for robotaxis in garages.
articles.body: You finally make it downtown for dinner, but now comes the real challenge. Finding somewhere to park. You circle the block once, then again. Before you know it, you're late and getting frustrated. Sound familiar? Well, Uber thinks it has a solution. The company just launched Uber Parking, a new feature that lets you reserve a parking spot directly through the Uber app before you even leave home. Yes, the same company that built its business around getting you into someone else's car now wants to help when you drive your own. And there's another interesting twist. Uber has plans for those parking garages that involve robotaxis. Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money. Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed. Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com. UBER LETS PARENTS WATCH TEEN RIDES LIVE Uber Parking lets you reserve a spot before you drive On Nov. 9, Uber announced the launch of Uber Parking, bringing parking reservations directly into its app. The feature follows Uber's acquisition of SpotHero, a popular parking reservation service. Through that deal, Uber gained access to a network of more than 13,000 parking garages, lots and valet locations across more than 400 cities in the United States and Canada. So, instead of driving around looking for parking, you can search for an available spot near your destination. You can also see the price upfront, making it easier to decide whether driving makes financial sense. For someone heading into the city for dinner or trying to get to an important appointment, that could save some aggravation. And if you've ever paid a small fortune to park somewhere, you'll probably appreciate being able to compare prices before arriving. How to book parking using the Uber app Uber has made the process pretty simple. You can book parking using the same app you already use to request a ride. Here's how it works: Once you've booked, your digital parking pass appears inside the Uber app. Depending on the location, you'll either scan a QR code or enter through a system that recognizes your license plate. Uber also says you can extend reservations through the app if you need more time. Cancellation policies vary by parking facility. Some reservations qualify for a full refund if canceled before the scheduled start time. Always check the booking terms before paying. One thing worth mentioning: Uber generally won't physically park your car for you. Unless you choose a valet location, you'll still be the one behind the wheel. FAKE E-ZPASS EMAIL THREATENS $100 FINE OVER UNPAID TOLL Where is Uber Parking available? Uber Parking launched in 15 U.S. cities on Nov. 9. Those cities are: Uber plans to expand the service into additional markets. However, there's an important detail here. Although SpotHero operates across more than 400 cities, Uber Parking has not yet expanded throughout that entire network. Also, the new feature is still rolling out. So, even if you're in one of the launch cities, you may not see the Parking icon immediately. First, make sure you're using the latest version of the Uber app. You can also visit SpotHero's website to search for parking in areas where the Uber feature is unavailable. Uber One members can earn 10% back on parking Here's a little bonus if you already pay for Uber One. Uber says eligible members can earn 10% back in Uber One credits on qualifying parking reservations once their parking session is complete. You can use those credits toward future eligible Uber rides or Uber Eats orders. For example, if you spend $30 on a qualifying parking reservation, you could earn $3 in Uber One credits. That may not sound like a fortune. However, if you're regularly parking downtown, those credits could add up. Just keep in mind that the 10% reward only applies to eligible reservations. You also need an active Uber One membership to qualify and redeem the credits. And remember, these are Uber credits rather than cash back to your bank account. Before booking, compare the total parking price with other nearby options. A cheaper garage could still save you more money than the rewards you'd earn. Why Uber wants parking garages for robotaxis Uber also sees parking garages as part of its future robotaxi business. Think about it. When a driverless taxi drops someone off, what happens next? If another passenger needs a ride nearby, that's easy enough. But what happens when nobody needs the car? Does it keep driving around until another request comes in? That could mean more empty vehicles on already crowded streets. Uber is reportedly exploring ways to use parking facilities as waiting areas for autonomous vehicles. Instead of driving around without passengers, robotaxis could pull into nearby garages and wait for their next assignment. Then, when someone requests a ride, the vehicle could head out to pick them up. Uber believes that approach could reduce unnecessary driving and help lower operating costs. There's another potential benefit. Keeping autonomous vehicles in nearby facilities could make it easier to have them ready when demand increases. However, this remains a developing plan. Uber has not announced that every SpotHero garage will accommodate robotaxis, and the company has not provided a timeline for a broad rollout of these facilities. For now, the immediate focus remains helping people find parking for their own cars. Uber wants to be part of your trip even when you drive There's something else worth paying attention to here. For years, Uber built its business around giving people an alternative to driving. Now, the company wants you opening its app even when you plan to take your own car. Let's say you're going downtown for dinner. You could check the price of an Uber ride. Then, you could compare that with the cost of driving and parking. If driving looks cheaper, you can reserve a space through Uber. If taking a ride makes more sense, you can book that instead. Either way, Uber stays part of your plans. And as autonomous vehicles become more common, the company could eventually use that same parking network to support its robotaxi partners. It's an interesting strategy, especially as Uber looks for more ways to keep people using its app. What this means to you The biggest benefit is pretty straightforward. You may be able to reserve parking before leaving home and spend less time driving around looking for an available spot. That could be especially useful when you're heading somewhere unfamiliar or trying to make a flight. However, there are a few things I'd recommend checking before you book. 1. Compare the total parking price Don't assume Uber offers the lowest rate. Check the final price against other parking options before paying. Also, make sure your reservation covers the time you'll actually need. 2. Check the garage entrance and restrictions Some parking garages have height limits. If you drive a larger SUV or truck, check those restrictions before booking. Also, confirm the exact entrance address, which may differ from the garage's street address. 3. Review the cancellation policy Some parking reservations can be canceled for free before they begin, but the rules vary by location. Review the specific garage's cancellation terms before booking. Once your reservation starts, Uber says it can no longer be canceled or refunded. 4. Watch out for parking QR code scams Some garages use QR codes for entry. That's convenient, but criminals have also placed fake QR codes on parking meters to trick drivers into visiting fraudulent payment websites. Use the parking pass provided directly through your Uber app rather than scanning an unfamiliar sticker. We've previously reported on how criminals use fake parking QR codes to steal money. 5. Save your car's location before walking away Even with a reservation, finding your car afterward can still be a headache. Fortunately, Google Maps and Apple Maps have tools that can help you remember where you parked. Our guide to finding your parked car with Maps explains how to set them up. Kurt's key takeaways I think Uber is onto something here. Who hasn't wasted time driving around looking for parking, especially when you're already running late? Being able to reserve a spot before leaving home sounds pretty convenient. Of course, I'd want to make sure I'm getting a good price. But what really caught my attention is Uber's plan to use parking garages for robotaxis. Having driverless cars park between rides makes sense, especially if it means fewer empty vehicles clogging up our streets. Still, I wonder what happens when those garages start filling up with robotaxis. Will there be enough room for the rest of us? That's something I'll be watching as this technology takes off. Would you trust Uber to handle your parking reservations, or do you worry that parking garages could eventually become crowded with robotaxis, leaving fewer spaces for the rest of us? articles.title: Exclusive: Daniel Ek backs AI researcher's fusion power startup. Here's what they're building. | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher. Here's what the startup is building.
articles.body:
Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a stealthy fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher who is taking a different approach to developing a fusion power plant.

The U.K.-based startup was founded in February, though sources told TechCrunch that the founder, Nantas Nardelli, has been working on the idea for longer. The people asked not to be identified because the information isn’t public. Bloomberg first reported Ek’s backing of Europa Fusion.

Nardelli has extensive experience in the AI world, having previously worked at Google DeepMind, Facebook AI Research, and Microsoft Research Cambridge. Recently, he was head of machine learning at Pacific Fusion , the fusion power startup based in Fremont, California.

Pacific Fusion recently broke ground on a demonstration facility in New Mexico. Like most fusion startups of its size , Pacific Fusion leans heavily on physical devices to test its theories and improve its simulations.

Nardelli apparently didn’t agree with the focus on hardware, instead thinking that fusion startups should invest in a more simulation- and data-heavy approach, a source familiar with his thinking told TechCrunch.

Like Pacific Fusion, Europa Fusion will pursue a pulsed-power approach to fusion. Pulsed-power reactors use massive, perfectly timed surges of electrical current to compress fuel targets until the atoms inside fuse and release energy.

Fusion power has the potential to be a significant energy source in the coming decades, but to date, no one has built a power plant capable of supplying electricity to the grid. If fusion power becomes commercially viable, though, it could possibly be a significant source of carbon-free power that draws on nearly limitless fuel supplies. The technology also has the potential to alleviate concerns about AI’s energy consumption.

Fusion’s ability to generate electricity without exacerbating climate change apparently drove Nardelli’s pivot from AI.

“My original background is in electronics and control engineering,” he wrote on his website . “I used to build robots for a living. One day I’ll be back to that, but it’s time to fix climate change for good.”

articles.title: Startup sues Apple in India over tap-to-share contacts feature | TechCrunch
articles.summary: A U.S. startup is seeking $162 million in damages and an injunction to impact iPhone and Apple Watch imports to India.
articles.body:
Apple is being sued in India by a U.S.-based startup that alleges the iPhone maker’s NameDrop feature, which lets users share contact information by bringing devices close together, infringes its patented technology.

GG Technologies, the startup behind StayTouch , an app that lets users exchange contact details by bringing their phones close together, is seeking ₹15 billion (about $161.86 million) in damages and an injunction against Apple, per court documents reviewed by TechCrunch.

Santa Monica-headquartered GG Technologies filed the lawsuit in India in October after mediation proceedings initiated in April failed in September, the startup told TechCrunch. Pre-institution mediation is generally required before filing commercial lawsuits in India. The company also sued Apple in the U.S. in April over related patent infringement claims.

In its 781-page court filing in the Bombay High Court, GG Technologies alleged that Apple’s NameDrop infringes its Indian patent on technology that helps phones exchange contact details with nearby devices without requiring manual pairing. The company launched StayTouch in 2019, the same year it first sought patent protection for the technology in the U.S. It filed its Indian patent application in 2021 and received the patent in July 2024.

Apple introduced NameDrop as part of iOS 17 in June 2023. The feature debuted on iPhones later that year, with support for compatible Apple Watches arriving in October through watchOS 10.1.

“We are seeking an injunction to restrict the usage of the NameDrop feature which is native to iOS,” GG Technologies told TechCrunch. GG Technologies urged the court in its filing to restrict Apple from selling or importing iPhones and Apple Watches preloaded with NameDrop in India. The case has yet to be listed for a hearing.

In the U.S., the International Trade Commission opened an investigation into Apple’s alleged patent infringement in August, following a complaint from GG Technologies. The startup is seeking an order that could block imports of infringing Apple devices into the country, along with restrictions on their sale.

Founded in 2018 by Gaurav Goel, a graduate of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi and a former Goldman Sachs investment banker, GG Technologies developed StayTouch as an alternative to exchanging business cards. The app is available on iOS and Android .

Apple did not respond to a request for comment.

India has become increasingly important to Apple, both as a fast-growing consumer market and a major manufacturing hub outside China . The Cupertino company has expanded its retail presence in the South Asian nation, where iPhones still account for less than 10% of smartphone shipments, giving considerable room for growth.

articles.title: TechCrunch Mobility: A/B testing robots vs. humans
articles.summary: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and, now more than ever, the role AI is playing in it.
articles.body:
Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility , your hub for the future of transportation and, now more than ever, the role AI is playing in it. To get this in your inbox, sign up here for free — just click TechCrunch Mobility !

Waymo pulling its robotaxis off freeways (again) and Zoox robotaxis launching on the Uber app illustrate the push and pull between progress and setbacks in the autonomous vehicle industry.

There are signs of growth. For instance, Tesla has now surpassed Waymo in Texas in the number of robotaxis registered with the state (Tesla has 1,507 and Waymo has 1,345). But does that translate to market dominance?

A better metric, if we’re trying to gauge who is leading, would be commercial driverless miles. And if we’re measuring cost-efficiency, another useful metric would be driverless miles per vehicle. By those measures, Waymo is still ahead, based on data available to me. But with Waymo’s recent freeways setback and Tesla’s push to expand its robotaxi fleet with Cybercabs, that lead could shrink.

Not that there needs to be a winner, by the way. Transportation is deeply fragmented, and there is room for multiple players in the U.S., not to mention the rest of the world.

A recent discussion with my Autonocast co-host Ed Niedermeyer, whose book, “Elon Take the Wheel,” comes out December 1, got me thinking about how Las Vegas could soon become a real world A/B test of sorts for human-driven vs. autonomous ride-hailing services.

Uber, as mentioned above, just added Zoox to its ride-hailing app in Las Vegas. For now, riders don’t have much of a choice. Uber customers can increase their chances of getting a Zoox robotaxi, and they can always decline a robot ride. But they can’t directly select a robotaxi. Instead, Uber riders will be matched with one if it’s available.

Uber said that will soon change. The company plans to introduce a dedicated autonomous option in its app as “availability and reliability improve,” Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said during the company’s third-quarter earnings call in November.

Las Vegas will also become the first U.S. city where riders can access two fully driverless partners through the Uber app, he said. (Hyundai’s self-driving subsidiary Motional is also an Uber partner.)

That would give Uber riders a meaningful choice: a human driver or a robotaxi, and potentially even which autonomous service to use. And it could offer a revealing look at what customers actually prefer when given that choice. Price could tip the balance, too.

It makes me wonder whether Las Vegas will become the next battleground for organized labor as robotaxis begin competing directly with human drivers.

You might have seen the Wall Street Journal scoop that General Motors is working with an executive search firm to identify possible candidates to replace CEO Mary Barra . Rumors of her imminent departure have swirled for months, but this time there appears to be real work happening behind the scenes.

I reached out to a few little birds to learn more and here’s what they’re telling me. And, for the record, GM declined to comment.

GM has hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles, according to one source, who noted it’s possible that the board has other executive search firms working on this as well. The board is taking a two-track approach to its search, which is occurring simultaneously.

The first is focused on traditional yet transformative automotive CEOs. One name that has come up from the executive search firm is José Muñoz, who is president and CEO of Hyundai. The board is also interested in someone less traditional. The firm has apparently floated names like Doug Field, who recently became CEO of Mind Robotics, and Larry Culp of GE, according to a source with direct information.

There are internal GM folks who are also in the mix, including Sterling Anderson, co-founder of self-driving trucks company Aurora who became chief product officer at GM in May 2025, and Paul Jacobson, the company’s executive vice president and chief financial officer.

Got a tip for us? Email Kirsten Korosec at [email protected] .

Elysian Aircraft , the Dutch aerospace company developing aviation electrification technologies, raised €12 million in private and public funding from FideFlux, SecFund, and ROM InWest, as well as from individual investors and family offices.

Mahindra Last Mile Mobility , an electric three-wheeler business under Mahindra & Mahindra, is looking at an IPO in about 18 months, per Bloomberg .

Numa , a startup developing an AI operating system for dealerships, raised a $45 million Series C round led by New York-based Blue Cloud Ventures. Threshold Ventures, Costanoa, Touring Capital, Gradient Ventures, and Tokio Marine Future Fund also participated.

Stark Future , a European electric motorcycle company, raised at least €150 million in equity, Reuters reported. The raise was led by Highland Europe, alongside Morgan Stanley Investment Management’s 1GT and Axon Partners Group.

Vincue , an automotive tech company that sells software to dealerships, raised $93 million in a round led by Wavecrest Growth Partners, with continued backing from FM Capital.

Also , the electric micromobility startup that spun out of Rivian last year, has paused deliveries of its new e-bike over problems with its software and batteries, The Verge reported .

Edmunds released new data that found the average new vehicle is selling for a record $50,087.

Redwood Materials is using computer vision and machine learning to identify and sort batteries by chemistry before they’re fed into the company’s rotary calciner — a massive cylindrical industrial furnace used to process 40,000 metric tons of raw feedstock a year.

Tesla said it will spend about $3.3 billion to expand its Berlin gigafactory to produce Cybercabs — yet another signal of the company’s global autonomy ambitions.

Over the weekend, Tesla invited “select customers” to preorder the company’s autonomous, golden Cybercab “for personal use.” The Cybercab is priced at $29,990, but there is a lot more to ownership. The company will charge owners $299 a month to use the vehicles, delivery will only occur in a handful of cities, and operations will be limited to specific locations.

Uber opened its ride-hailing service to children as young as 10 in three U.S. cities. Uber already has a service for teenagers. If this program proves successful, it would open Uber up to another market of customers: busy families.

Meanwhile, Uber said it’s notifying close to 150,000 drivers that their personal information was stolen in an October data breach.

Zipline continues to scale its autonomous drone delivery business, this time in its partnership with Uber. The companies had previously announced a partnership for drones to deliver for Uber Eats, but it officially launched this week in a Houston suburb. The aim is a big one: Uber and Zipline say they aim to make 1 million deliveries a day using the startup’s drones by the end of 2029.

I had a chance to catch up with (and interview) Ro Gupta , the head of Woven Capital — Toyota’s growth fund.

I’ve known Gupta for years; we first met when I worked at Fortune and he had a startup called Carmera. A lot has happened since those AV 1.0 days, and Gupta caught us up on this next era of AV innovation and where Toyota is interested in investing. It’s not enough to simply state “AI.” There’s more to it than that. Take a listen .

articles.title: Uber now lets you book rides that record the drive by default | TechCrunch

articles.body:
Uber is piloting a new feature in the U.S. that offers rides in which drivers have enabled the company’s recording feature, Record My Ride.

The option, which uses the front camera of the Uber driver’s phone to record the entire drive, will show up as “Recorded Rides” in the app.

The ride-hailing company is starting the pilot in Baltimore, Raleigh, Indianapolis, and St. Louis and will expand to more locations later.

Uber said it is testing recorded rides specifically for rides booked at late night or those involving teens. Earlier this year, it introduced a live video streaming feature for rides booked for teenagers . In another test, the company had enabled audio recording for late night trips in some cities.

The company is also testing a feature that will turn on recording when the app detects the ride going off-course, or when the vehicle might have had an accident.

The company said drivers can opt out of recording through the Settings panel. Similarly, riders can also decline permission to record their rides via an in-app notification.

articles.title: Sierra doubles valuation to $30B within six months as demand for AI in CX takes off | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Enterprise customer experience company Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, said on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round.
articles.body:
Enterprise customer experience company Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, said on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles the company’s valuation to $30 billion. The new raise comes within six months of its previous round, which valued the company at $15 billion .

The new round was led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors who have led previous rounds, including Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks, GV, and Tiger Global.

Enterprise automation is among the few areas where AI has seen rapid adoption. Sierra said that it currently serves almost 50% of Fortune 50 companies, and its clients include BNY, HSBC, Singtel, Wells Fargo, JPMorganChase, Pearson, Next, and Cox Automotive. The company late last month said its outcome-based pricing model has helped it double its run-rate revenue to $400 million within five months .

That said, Sierra is working along similar lines as other customer experience players in the market, which is creating a platform to build agents and partner with model developers to provide choices to enterprises. As personal and work agents interact with enterprise systems, Sierra is also working on creating protocol definitions for agents with companies like Meta, Stripe, and Walmart.

Sierra will use the fresh cash build to its technology stack to layer agents for servicing, and hire more sales folks to sign and maintain enterprise contracts faster than its rivals.

Startups operating in the CX space have seen multi-million-dollar rounds come their way with soaring valuations. Voice AI company ElevenLabs is now valued at $22 billion; Decagon is valued at $4.5 billion ; Wonderful is valued at $5 billion ; and Parloa is valued at $3 billion . Multiple other startups have scored investments of more than $100 million.

During the HumanX conference in Amsterdam in September, Sierra co-founder Clay Bavor argued that despite the popular belief that AI-powered CX companies are replacing humans in contact centers, a majority of its customers are reassigning roles to existing employees.
